'''Copper Ore''' can be refined into [[Copper]] in a [[Smelter]].

Two Copper can be further processed at a [[Forge]] with [[Tin]] to yield [[Bronze]].

== Availability ==
It can be mined from [[Copper Deposit]]s which can be found in [[Black Forest]] [[biomes]] using any [[Pickaxes (skill)|Pickaxe]]. Such deposits have subtle bronze-colored streaks that reflect the sunlight. It is the only visual feature that distinguishes them from typical stone boulders.

Copper deposits are generated in a large size which extends down into the ground, so digging deep underneath the surface is necessary to fully extract a single deposit.

== Notes ==
* A way of farming Copper is to dig the earth all around the deposit until it crumbles on itself into Copper Ores. 
* Like other metals, Copper Ore cannot be teleported without a [[Portal stone]].
* The attacks of a [[Troll]], despite being harmless to normal terrain, cause immense damage to Copper Ore. If the player has no pickaxe or simply yearns for a change from their usual monotonous mining method, a Troll can make for a great alternative.

[[File:Building screenshot.jpg|thumb|A player building a house]] {{Quote|Raise your own viking mead halls, houses, castles, and more with our powerful construction interface. From knarrs to imposing warships, build legendary vessels to conquer the seas and discover new lands.https://www.valheimgame.com/home/#anchor2}} Valheim features an extensive '''building''' system that can be utilized to design structures to meet the demands of any discriminating warrior. In addition to humble homes and outposts, players also use this building interface to make enormous bases, elaborate works of art, defenses against the [[Creatures]] of Valheim, and unique tools to aid in their survival. Starting out with simple wooden building components, players will eventually gain access to the ability to create stronger structures with various materials, including stone and metal. == Basics == You can build using a [[Hammer]] within the working area of a [[Workbench]]. * Press [1-8] to select the hammer in the hotbar slot * Press [RMB] to open the build menu * Press [Q/E] to switch [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] category * Press [LMB] to chose [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]], and place it * Press [Middle Mouse Button] to remove [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Scroll the mouse to rotate the [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Hold [Shift] to temporarily disable snapping * Hold [Shift] then [Middle Mouse Button] to select [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you are looking at. There are various crafting stations required to be nearby to place certain [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. These include the following: * The [[Workbench]], required to place most [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you have unlocked from the beginning or early on, and some late [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. The Workbench is immediately available and costs 10 ordinary wood to build. * The [[Forge]], required to place most building parts containing metals. The Forge requires [[copper]] to build, and becomes available once the player can mine and refine [[Copper Ore]]. * The [[Stonecutter]], required to place building parts created out of stone, such as the stone walls some abandoned buildings are made out of. The Stonecutter requires [[iron]] to build, and becomes available once the player can collect and refine [[Scrap Iron]]. * The [[Artisan Table]], required to build some crafting stations that as of Patch 0.142.6 are at the end of implemented progression. The Artisan Table requires [[Dragon Tear|Dragon Tears]] to build, which must be obtained by defeating the fourth boss, [[Moder]] the dragon. == Snap building == Most building components can snap to each other. This allows for quick and easy building, but can be temporarily disabled by holding the appropriate key or button. By default, this is L-Shift on mouse and keyboard, and LT+LB on controller. == Structural integrity == {{Main|Building stability}} If there is not enough support, the building pieces will fall down. You may reinforce the building with walls, beams, and poles. When you move the cursor to the building piece, it shows a color range from blue, to green, to red. Blue indicates that the part is as stable as it can be, as dictated by its material. The closer to red on the spectrum, the less stable the part. Attempting to place additional pieces onto one that is fully red may result in the new part breaking off and dropping the resources used to construct it unless the new part has lower stability requirements. The stability of an individual building piece is determined by its material, the stability of the piece it's anchored to and its position relative to it, each additional piece inheriting a fraction of the previous piece's stability. A directly vertical pole of [[Wood]] or [[Stone]] can rise 16 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Wood Wall]], [[Wood Wall Half]], [[Stone Wall 1x1]], [[Stone Wall 2x1]], [[Stone Wall 4x2]], [[Wood Pole 1 m]], [[Wood Pole 2 m]], [[Stone Pillar]]. A directly vertical pole of [[Corewood]] Logs can rise 24 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Log Pole 4 m]] and [[Log Pole 2 m]]. A directly vertical [[Wood Iron Pole]] can rise up to 50 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. Trees, including those planted by the player, will effectively function as "the ground" for support purposes, allowing for extremely high construction. [[File:Structure integrity.png|thumb|Found on [https://www.reddit.com/r/valheim/comments/lqsxki/updated_psa_structural_support_details/ Reddit /Valheim], thanks to [https://www.reddit.com/user/ToddGeorgeKelly/ user/ToddGeorgeKelly/]]] In order to keep tall structures stable, the tallest point should be reinforced by supports that create the shortest and most vertical path possible down to the ground. It is worth considering raising the terrain as much as possible below a structure, such that the floor and walls are 100% stable (highlighted in blue when moused over). Boulders are also considered terrain when calculating stability, so parts that intersect them are considered grounded. == Decay == If wooden building sections are not covered during rain, are not linked to a roof, or are submerged in water, they will decay to a maximum of 50% durability and will seem rotting until fixed. When exposed to rain, defensive structures do not rot decay. Stone, black marble, and crystal structures will not decay when wet or submerged. Building the desired structure's roof first, with the appropriate supports and foundation in place, will aid with constructions lasting days or weeks if rain is a worry. == Damage == Player, monster, and creature attacks can all damage structures. Defensive structures will also receive minor damage while causing harm to creatures that come into contact with them. Aggressive creatures are drawn to and hostile toward all light sources (excluding Jack-o-turnips) and crafting stations, and will try to break them if not attacking a player. == Repair == You can repair building parts that seem to be decaying or damaged with a [[Hammer]]. This does not cost any resources, but does consume stamina. The player must be in range of a crafting station that corresponds to the part being repaired, e.g. a [[Workbench]] when repairing a wooden part, or a [[Stonecutter]] for a stone part. == Abandoned buildings == These structures are a type of [[point of interest]] that can be found to naturally occur in the world. The size, layout, and materials these structures are made of can vary greatly as each is generated from random templates. There are different types of abandoned structures such as Abandoned Cabins, Abandoned Towers, Abandoned Farms just to name a few. These abandoned and generated structures can contain things such as chests with items specific to the biome, monsters (usually [[Skeleton]]s), [[:Category:Creature spawner|monster spawner]]s, and [[wikipedia:Vegvísir|Vegvisir]]s to mark the nearest boss altar for that biome. In the Meadows/Black Forest biome, they can also contain naturally spawning [[Beehive]]s, which will drop a [[Queen Bee]] and sometimes [[Honey]] when destroyed. Players should approach abandoned villages with caution since some villages have been reoccupied by [[Draugr]] and [[Draugr Elite]] who will attack the player on sight. These [[Draugr village|Draugr Villages]] can be identified by partial walls of sharp logs and the buzzing of the [[Creature spawner|spawners]] inside several of the buildings as well as a general miasma and the presence of Draugr both inside and outside the structures. They almost always have a large Mead Hall building that cannot be found anywhere else. There may also be a sentry in a tower armed with a bow who will snipe anything that comes near. == Player base and blocking spawning == {{Main|Player base}} Building certain structures considered to be 'player base' will have the following effects in a radius around them: * Prevent [[creatures|creature]] spawning * Prevent items dropped on the ground from despawning after 1 hour (unless submerged) * Enable player base [[events]] to occur For a full list of player base structures, see [[player base]]. == Base building strategies == [[File:Mordheim server - Guild Castle.jpg|thumb|850x850px]] * Building your outposts in close proximity to '''several biome borders''' grants access to varied resources and allows you to observe the territorial in-fighting of different creatures (complete with loot strewn across the terrain), but can also be dangerous. * Many types of '''defenses''' are possible, both in the form of built objects and altered terrain: ** Creatures cannot dig through terrain, making '''"terrain walls" effectively impenetrable''' to them. Thus the perfect defense is built either with a hoe and a pile of rocks, any pickaxe or ideally a combination of the two. Be warned that terrain alterations may cause stutter just as placing objects does (press F2 to check the number of "instances" loaded). ** A hoe can be used to raise terrain while you're standing on it, allowing you to quickly erect a '''pillar''' to stand on and shoot melee enemies below. Beware that you need a workbench nearby to do this. With practice this is possible during combat. ** Most creatures never jump down from ledges (Fenring and Blobs are exceptions). A '''deep pit''' (around 3 "blocks") is also largely safe, and you can shoot enemies coming close to the ledge. Flying creatures may attack from above if you don't build a roof, however. ** Gates can be destroyed, but '''gaps''' the player jumps over when entering or exiting the base cannot. This trick can be inconvenient, however. Also note that you can '''scale steep terrain''' walls by sprinting and jump-spamming, especially when moving towards a crease (corner) for better traction, while most creatures cannot. ** The most '''FPS-efficient method of defense''' is to build on a few terrain pillars. This minimizes terrain alteration "instances" yet allows you to ignore enemies running around outside, especially if the base entrance requires a quick hop to get on. Note that returning terrain to its roughly native height doesn't remove the FPS hit (unless a true "undo terrain changes" tool is added to the game). ** Workbenches (and campfires) '''disallow enemy spawns''' in their radius, making them surprisingly useful defensive tools. You can hide these in the outer perimeter of your walls or in small pits covered with a few floor tiles to make an area safer. Workbenches also stop dropped items from de-spawning over time, however. ** Doors and gates can be used to create a '''toggle-able bridge''' for carts. Another option to defend your bridge is to hang a gate from a support above it and attach the floor piece to the gate with small gaps on the sides, causing the floor to disappear if the gate is destroyed. ** You can place '''gates in the water''' to block enemies, who will be unable to attack the gates, yet allow boats to pass when opened. * The '''"Level Ground"''' option for the hoe uses the terrain height directly underneath you as the target altitude, though if you hold Shift while clicking it'll use the altitude of the terrain you're pointing at instead. Using this knowledge well may save you a lot of stone and work while landscaping as it only expends stamina and hoe durability. * You can also build a '''"gangplank"''' for enemies to walk on, above your pit base, and put a campfire on it so they'll kill themselves, then catch the loot when it drops down. * Combining a moat with a plateau-based outpost is an interesting option. Any objects within this free space will cause the "''Needs more room to grow"'' status. Crops require unobstructed view of the sky. Any structures built over a crop will cause the ''"Needs an open sky"'' status, regardless of how high the structure is above the crop. Unique among crops - Vineberry vines need to be 1 away from a flat built wall to climb. It can cross over Window or door openings, but any overhang or break in the wall will stop its growth. The '''Ocean''' is a [[Biomes|biome]] made up of, much like examples in real life, a vast body of water. It is only realistically accessible by [[boats]], as swimming out from the safety of the shore quickly depletes [[stamina]] and leads to drowning. In many ways, the Ocean acts as less its own dedicated biome, per se, and more a vehicle for player exploration.

Currently the biome only features the elusive and destructive [[Serpent]] enemy as well as the even more elusive [[Leviathan]], a hulking shelled creature covered in shrubbery, algae, and barnacles. These two creatures are the sole way for players to gather [[Serpent Scale|Serpent scales]] and [[Chitin]], respectively.

== Availability ==
Each mined barnacle has a 10% chance to trigger the Leviathan's retreat, signaled by a howl sound. Make sure to have a nearby [[Boats|boat]] or land to fall back to when it begins to sink.

'''Leviathans''' are passive [[creatures]] found in [[Ocean|Oceans]]. They are massive rock-type beings that have a 10% chance of submerging each time their [[Abyssal Barnacle]]s are damaged.

Leviathans themselves are immovable and indestructible; only the barnacles on their back can be destroyed by mining them.

It is not possible to build on Leviathans. 

===Drops===
Each [[Abyssal Barnacle]] drops the following when mined:
{{drop table|
{{drop row|item=Chitin| 0star=3-4}}
|stars=0}}
See their [[Abyssal Barnacle|main page]] for details on how to mine the barnacles.

Each time a barnacle is hit, there is a 10% chance that the leviathan will be disturbed (indicated by it shaking and emitting noise). Once 20 seconds have passed after it is first disturbed, it will begin permanently submerging into the ocean (accompanied by much more shaking and noises). During those 20 seconds, further hits still have a 10% chance to trigger additional shaking.

It takes roughly 25 seconds from the start of the leviathan's submersion process until its entire body is below the waterline. During the first few seconds it actually raises its body up higher, then slowly begins accelerating downward, eventually moving faster than 1 m/s.

=== Spawning===
Leviathans are spawned upon world generation and do not respawn once they have retreated below the depths of the ocean.

They have 1% chance of appearing on each full Ocean [[Spawn zones|zone]] and require at least 30 meters depth.

Chitin can be endlessly obtained this way, although the required bait can be difficult to obtain.
* To cheese the Leviathan, you can simply log out when it starts sinking. When you log back in, the Leviathan is no longer sinking. This is the only known way to fully mine a Leviathan.

== Trivia ==
* The Leviathan in Valheim is based on the [[wikipedia:Hafgufa|Hafgufa]] from Norse Mythology, and the game is faithful to their original appearance as a large creature that was mistaken for an island. The island is only its shell while the rest of the Hafgufa resides below.
* The ''actual'' [[wikipedia:Leviathan|Leviathan]] is more akin to Valheim's [[Serpent]].
* During [[Day and Night Cycle|night time]], its two glowing eyes can be seen underwater.
* Their underside lacks any distinct features and detail. This is likely intended from a development standpoint because players are only supposed to see the top part of them that is visible above water.

Pine trees produce [[Wood]] and [[Corewood]] when destroyed. The yield of each type of wood appears to be random, however, a pine tree will always drop 30 pieces of wood total.

[[Pine Cone|Pine cones]] can be planted with a [[cultivator]] to grow more Pine. Pine trees can be planted in the [[Meadows]]. The low drop rate on the Pine Cones makes Pine, and thus Corewood, unsustainable.

'''Crafting''' is the process of converting and combining [[materials]] to create new [[items]]. 

Some basic items can be crafted in the player inventory, but most items require a dedicated crafting station such as a [[Workbench]] or [[Forge]]. Most gear can also be upgraded to a higher quality, increasing its durability and other aspects.

== Crafting mechanics ==
[[File:Crafting-a-Cultivator.jpg|thumb|The crafting interface of a level 2 Forge, showing the recipe of a [[Cultivator]]. The station level is shown within the star in the top right. The craft tab allows crafting new items, whereas the upgrade tab allows upgrading gear currently in the inventory.]]

Crafting an item at a crafting station requires having the appropriate materials in the [[inventory]], as well as an available slot in the inventory for the result.

Gear that has durability can be repaired for free using the hammer icon at the side of the crafting interface at the crafting station where it was crafted (excluding the inventory). Gear that requires a higher station level to be crafed can also only be repaired at a station at that level, upgrading it does not increase this requirement.

Most weapons, tools and armors can be upgraded to higher qualities, often up to 3 times to a quality of 4. Each upgrade level requires a higher station level. Upgrading increases the durability of the item, and also improves its properties: weapons deal higher damage, while armors provide more [[Armor]]. Upgrading costs a considerable amount of resources and can double or triple the crafting cost of a given item over its cost at quality 1.

For example, the [[Troll Leather Tunic]] requires a level 2 Workbench to be crafted. Thus, it cannot be repaired at a level 1 Workbench. Upgrading it to quality 2 requires a level 3 Workbench, to quality 3 a level 4 Workbench, etc. It initially costs 6 [[Troll Hide]] to craft, but upgrading it to quality 4 costs an additional 11 Troll Hide for a total of 17.

== Usage ==
The '''Shield generator''' dome protects the player and structures within:
* Protects from [[Rain]], prevents players from getting the [[Wet Effect]] and structures from being damaged. (Similar to the [[Shelter Effect]])
* Protects from [[Cinder rain]] in [[Ashlands]], prevents the structure from catching on fire from falling cinder.
* Protects against incoming projectiles such as [[Creatures]] attacks.
* Protects against [[Lava]] balls randomly coming from lava lakes, useful when mining [[Flametal Ore Vein]]s close to lava edge.

== Behavior ==
The Shield generator can be built upon solid ground, [[Cage Structures|Cage]], [[Stone Structures|Stone]], [[Black Marble Structures|Black marble]] or [[Grausten Structures|Grausten]] structures.

The radius of effect is 30 meters in a spherical area centered on the Shield generator.

The generator can hold up to 10 [[Bone Fragments]] or [[Charred Bone]] as fuel and consumes one fuel per 500 damage. Damage will occur when a projectile with an origin outside the radius of effect comes into contact with the shield edge, absorbing the projectile in the process. These absorbed projectiles include the environmental Cinders, and any combat projectiles, ranged or magical, produced by players or creatures. Although the effects of Rain are nullified by the shield, this effect will not cause damage, or consume fuel of the shield generator.

The radius of two or more shields overlapping will result in their intersection combining, allowing multiple shields to be chained together into a larger shield.

== Trivia ==
* Due to the shield determining whether to block an incoming projectile based on its origin position, it is possible for the player to fire a projectile from within the shielded region, and as it exits and re-enters the region, will not be absorbed by the shield.
* Though the effects of Rain are nullified, the Shield generator will not protect [[Fire Effect]] yielding structures from being extinguished, still requiring Shelter.

== Tips ==
* The Shield generator is useful for [[Farming (Skill)|Farming]], where most crops must not be placed under Shelter, normally forcing the player to farm under the effects of rain.

'''Frost Foundry''' is a structure used to craft in the [[Deep North]]. It hardens [[Moulds|Casts]] into finished Deep North weapons, armor, shields, staffs and the {{Item link|Intricate Key}}.

==Building==
The Frost Foundry is found in the Crafting category of the [[Hammer]] and requires a nearby [[Workbench]] to build. It cannot be placed in water or on sloped surfaces. It costs:
* {{Item link|Iron|15}}
* {{Item link|Stone|20}}
* {{Item link|Frostcore|10}}

It has 500 durability. It is resistant to pierce and frost damage, weak to chop damage, and immune to poison and spirit damage.

==Usage==
It can be fueled with [[Liquid Frost]], which is made in the [[Frigid Kiln]]. It holds up to 20 Liquid Frost, and each unit lasts 10 seconds. Fuel is only used while an unfinished cast is inside.

A [[Moulds|Cast]] can be placed at the center to create the final item. The Frost Foundry holds one cast at a time. The process consumes five Liquid Frost and takes 50 seconds. Finished items cannot burn if left inside. Items made in the Frost Foundry come out at full durability.

Casts are made at the [[Black Forge]] or the [[Galdr Table]], as listed below.
